title: 6.7.11 Fix the Broken Pseudocode: Dragging a Sprite
description: Repair half-finished pseudocode for dragging: give the mouse-up frame its own branch, put the velocity reset where it belongs, and stop a step jumping to itself.

steps.title: Repair the half-finished pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is what the finished feature should do, in plain English:

**1.** While the mouse is pressing: if the sprite is under the mouse, move the sprite to the mouse.

**2.** When the mouse is not pressing (it was let go): set the sprite velocity to zero, so it does not fly off.

**3.** Every path ends at the end of the frame. No step may send you back to itself.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the steps.

Someone charted picking the sprite up carefully, and stopped. Their pseudocode is already in `README.md`. **Press Run before changing anything**: three checks should be red. Read each red card against the plan above, then repair it. Do not start over. A new keyword for this repair: `ELSE` starts the branch for every other case. In a different program: `IF door is open` ... `ELSE` ... `END IF`. The ELSE belongs to the decision it lines up with, so close the inner decision first.

Renumber the lines if you like: every line just needs a number.

When it is green, trace this: the player presses the mouse somewhere empty, then drags across the sprite while still holding. Does your plan pick it up mid-drag? Should it?

Plain English is fine here. Press **Grade** above the editor: the AI reads what your steps mean and marks each Quest card green or red. Changing your text clears its marks, so press Grade again when you have finished editing.
hints: A sprite dragged around has picked up speed. What should happen to that speed when you let go?
The loop that repeats is draw() itself, not a line in this plan.

requirements.title: The frames where the mouse is up are handled
requirements.description: The pressing decision has a branch for when the mouse is not pressing.
requirements.hint: The frames where the mouse is up need their own branch (ELSE). Check where it sits: the inner decision closes first, then the ELSE belongs to the pressing decision.

requirements.title: The velocity reset happens on release only
requirements.description: The velocity is zeroed only on the frames where the mouse is up.
requirements.hint: A sprite still being dragged must not have its velocity zeroed. Which frames should do that?

requirements.title: Every step moves forward
requirements.description: No step sends you back to an earlier step. Moving the sprite is one ordinary step per frame.
requirements.hint: Look for a step that sends the flow back to itself: that is a hung game, written down.

requirements.title: Moving the sprite needs the sprite under the mouse
requirements.description: The sprite follows the mouse only inside the check for the sprite being under it.
requirements.hint: The sprite should follow the mouse only when the check about the sprite and the mouse is true.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([draw runs]) --> B{mouse pressing?}
  B -- yes --> C{sprite under the mouse?}
  C -- yes --> D[move the sprite to the mouse]
  C -- no --> Z([end of frame])
  D --> Z
  B -- no --> E[stop the sprite moving]
  E --> Z
planChart.caption: The finished drag. Releasing has its own branch, and the velocity reset sits on it.
